hypothesis: The kernel already assigns one warp to each target. Increasing each CTA from 8 to 16 target warps halves the CTA count for a given N and may reduce scheduling overhead; the larger CTA could also affect residency, so the controller must measure it.
notes: The existing kernel retains its N-tail and self-pair handling, softening for coincident positions, warp reductions, and single-lane writes of the complete particle state. No correctness or speed result is claimed for this launch configuration; the controller should check correctness before timing.
transformations: Set block to 512 threads and items_per_block to 16, keeping items_per_block equal to block/32 for one target warp per warp.
